metadata.case_name: TANG YUET YI, A MINOR BY TIU KWAI KING, HER LAWFUL AND NATURAL MOTHER AND NEXT FRIEND v. EUNG MAN CHOW

injuries.description: Head laceration at right parietal region (dog bite wound)
source: physical examination revealed that the plaintiffs airway was patent. There were head laceration at right parietal region, left sided facial laceration, no bony tenderness, and good range of movement of the neck. Her chest wall showed deep laceration with exposure of soft tissue, but there was good air entry into her chest. There were left shoulder bruising, tender soft tissue, but her left elbow and left wrist were normal. The diagnosis was serious dog attack with multiple soft tissue injury.

injuries.description: Right occiput scalp dog bite wound down to subcutaneous layer
source: the plaintiff had multiple dog bite wounds over: her left face (measuring 2 x 1 cm in size), left chest wall (measuring 6 x 2 cm in size down to muscle level), left posterior shoulder (measuring 4 x 2 cm in size down to deltoid muscle) and right occiput scalp (measuring 3 x 0.5 cm in size down to subcutaneous layer).

injuries.icd_description: Open bite of shoulder or upper arm

injuries.description: Permanent scars (hypertrophic scars) on face, shoulder and left clavicular regions
injuries.body_part: face, shoulder and left clavicular regions
source: The scars cannot be removed. The plaintiff would have permanent scars on the face, shoulder and left clavicular regions.

It is recorded in the medical report prepared by Dr Ko Wai Shan dated 8 February 2017 that the scars of the plaintiff were found hypertrophic. She was put on pressure therapy with pressure garment and cica care. The hypertrophic scars responded fairly with treatment. Upon her latest return for assessment, most scars were flat and maturing. There was no functioning impairment by the scar. She was advised to continue with silicone and massage till the scars were mature.

manifestations.description: Obvious scars and deformities on various parts of her body
Hypertrophic scars over left arm and chest areas (improved, mostly flat and maturing)
Psychological trauma including being afraid of all kinds of dog and other animals including cats and birds
No functioning impairment by the scar

treatments_received.treatment: Radiographs (no fracture found) and initial assessment at Accident & Emergency Department of North District Hospital
source: After the incident, the plaintiff was sent to the Accident & Emergency Department of North District Hospital ("AED of NDH"). Radiographs were taken. No fracture was found. She was then sent to Department of Surgery of the Prince of Wales Hospital ("PWH") for further treatment.

treatments_received.treatment: Emergency operation for wounds toileting and suturing (10 October 2015)
source: Emergency operation for wounds toileting and suturing was performed on 10 October 2015. Postoperative recovery was smooth with daily wounds dressing and packing performed.
Postoperative recovery was smooth with daily wounds dressing and packing performed.

treatments_received.treatment: Course of antibiotics and rabies vaccinations
source: A course of antibiotics and rabies vaccinations were completed during her hospital stay.

treatments_received.treatment: Ophthalmologist consultation (no scleral or conjunctival injury)
source: Ophthalmologist was consulted and examination revealed no scleral or conjuntival injury.

treatments_received.treatment: Clinical psychologist consultation (assessment showed no significant acute stress reaction)
source: Clinical psychologist was consulted and assessment showed no significant acute stress reaction.

treatments_received.treatment: Pressure therapy with pressure garment and cica care
source: It is recorded in the medical report prepared by Dr Ko Wai Shan dated 8 February 2017 that the scars of the plaintiff were found hypertrophic. She was put on pressure therapy with pressure garment and cica care. The hypertrophic scars responded fairly with treatment.

treatments_received.treatment: Occupational therapy: pressure jacket with padding and mepliform sheet; final assessment and discharge recommendation
source: According to the occupational therapy report dated 3 August 2017, the plaintiff was provided with pressure jacket with padding and mepliform sheet. Final assessment of the Plaintiffs condition showed that her hypertrophic scars over left arm and chest areas were improved that closely resembled the colour of the rest of the body, normal capillary refill rate, flat, without pain nor itchiness with remaining minimal resistance upon manual pressure only. The plaintiff was recommended to apply mepliform on scar area by self at the time of discharge.

treatments_future.treatment: Intralesional steroid injections (about 10 injections at intervals of four weeks to three months)
source: The raised hypertrophic scars can be improved with intralesional steroid injections that the plaintiff needs about 10 injections at intervals of four weeks to three months.
The plaintiff may benefit from topical application of silicone gel.

treatments_future.treatment: Laser treatment for hyperpigmented scars (about 15 sessions)
source: The hyperpigmented scars can be improved with laser. The plaintiff needs about fifteen sessions of laser treatment.

treatments_future.treatment: Laser treatment for depressed scars (about 15 sessions at 2-3 month intervals)
source: The depressed scars can be treated with laser. The plaintiff needs treatment at two to three months interval for about 15 sessions.

treatments_future.treatment: Excision revision (revision surgery for the scalp) under local anaesthesia at skeletal maturity (age 18)
source: The hairiness scar on the scalp can be improved by excising the scar under local anesthesia when she reaches skeletal maturity at the age of 18.
treatments_future.vmis_procedure: Local excision or destruction of lesion or tissue of skin and subcutaneous tissue

treatments_future.treatment: Skin care products to alleviate itchiness of the scars for about two years
source: The plaintiff needs skin care products to alleviate itchiness of the scars for about two years.

treatments_future.treatment: Follow-up consultations (as claimed: 45 consultations in claim)
source: Follow-up Consultations: HK$1,000.00 x 45 HK$45,000.00

losses.description: Permanent scars on the face, shoulder and left clavicular regions; hypertrophic scars (some improved but permanent scarring remains)
